entry.title: Empirical Assessment of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status in TLS. Anticipating Q-day security concerns, major CDNs and cloud providers are migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC).
entry.summary:
Anticipating Q-day security concerns, major CDNs and cloud providers are migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). While existing literature benchmarks PQC performance, empirical research evaluating real-world adoption data remains scarce. We present an empirical assessment of PQC deployment across seven critical protocols (HTTPS, LDAPS, SMTPS, IMAP-SSL, POP3-SSL, TELNETS, and RDP) using 10,000 target IP addresses per protocol.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #post-quantum

entry.title: RoKoko: Lattice-based Succinct Arguments, a Committed Refinement
entry.summary:
We present RoKoko, a new lattice-based succinct argument system that achieves a linear-time prover alongside polylogarithmic communication and verifier complexity. Asymptotically, our construction improves upon RoK and Roll (ASIACRYPT 2025), the first post-quantum SNARK with $\tilde{O}(\lambda)$ proof size, by a multiplicative factor of $\Theta(\log \lambda)$. Practically, our system yields proofs of roughly $200$KB, while outperforming the state-of-the-art polynomial commitment scheme Greyhound (CRYPTO 2024) with a $100\times$ faster verification time, similar prover time, and competitive proof size.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Sonata: Certifying Canonical Openings in High-Arity Lattice Folding. Folding lets a prover certify a computation incrementally by combining committed instances into an accumulator.
entry.summary:
Folding lets a prover certify a computation incrementally by combining committed instances into an accumulator. In lattice-based folding, a linear combination of field values can change their canonical digit representations. Re-encoding the result gives the prover a short opening.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum
